mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is held constant above 5.00% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return is expected to be negative due to persistent higher real borrowing costs compressing equity discounting.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the 30-day rolling mean during qualifying periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An unexpected increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) above 200,000 jobs, not preceded by inflation acceleration (CPIAUCSL), predicts a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as labor market strength supports equity risk appetite.
regime_hint: Labor market strengthening without price pressures
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns do not outperform the 30-day rolling mean by at least 1.5% (p > 0.05 in two-sided test).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in industrial production (INDPRO) of at least 2% for three consecutive months predicts a positive S&P 20-day forward return as it signals resilient economic momentum and reduced recession risk.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO grows ≥ 2% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are flat or negative during qualifying INDPRO upswings (mean difference < 0).

mechanism_narrative: When consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) unexpectedly accelerates by more than 0.5 percentage points in a month, the S&P 60-day forward return is expected to be negative as investors anticipate tighter monetary policy and demand compression.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases by > 0.5pp in a single month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns do not fall below the prior 30-day forward mean during qualifying CPI spikes (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% triggers a positive S&P 5-day forward return as market anticipates rate cuts and accommodative policy, boosting equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 3.50% in a single month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns remain flat or negative during qualifying UNRATE declines (mean difference ≤ 0).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising retail sales (HOUST) above 2,000 units with no simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) suggests resilient consumer demand, predicting a positive 20-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 2,000 for two consecutive months and INDPRO > 1,000 for those months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns do not exceed the prior 10-day forward mean during qualifying periods (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in job openings (PAYEMS) below 7 million for three consecutive months indicates softening labor market conditions and predicts a negative S&P 60-day forward return as risk aversion rises.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the 30-day rolling mean during qualifying softening periods (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the ratio of industrial production to consumer price inflation (INDPRO / CPIAUCSL) exceeds 2.0 for two consecutive months, it suggests supply-side resilience and forecasts a positive 20-day forward return for the S&P 500.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO / CPIAUCSL > 2.0 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns do not beat the prior 10-day forward mean during qualifying ratios (p > 0.05).
